name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
credit: St. Hilary of Poitiers, illustration, Wikimedia Commons · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Hilary was born at Poitiers early in the fourth century, became bishop of his native city about 350, and died in the later 360s. His feast day gives its name to Hilary Term.
John Brownlie's notes say that four Latin hymns are attributed to him. One of them, the morning hymn Jam meta noctis transiit, is given here in Brownlie's English version of 1896.

poems.title: Gone are the shades of night
poems.author: St. Hilary of Poitiers
poems.note: Latin: Jam meta noctis transiit. Brownlie: one of four morning hymns attributed to St. Hilary.
poems.text:
Gone are the shades of night,
  The hours of rest are o'er;
New beauties sparkle bright,
  And heaven is light once more.

To Thee our prayers shall speed,
  O Lord of light divine;
Come to our utmost need,
  And in our darkness shine.

Spirit of love and light,
  May we Thine image know,
And in Thy glory bright,
  To full perfection grow.

Hear us, O Father blest,
  Hear us, O Christ the Son,
And Comforter the best,
  Now, and till life is done.
